name: What is the difference between MDF and solid wood baseboards?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between MDF and solid wood baseboards?

acceptedAnswer.text: MDF (medium-density fiberboard) is smooth, uniform, and very budget-friendly, making it a great choice for paint-grade trim in dry living spaces. However, it swells permanently if exposed to standing water. Solid wood or finger-jointed pine costs more but handles minor moisture and physical bumps better, holds nails securely, and cuts cleanly. For high-moisture rooms like bathrooms, laundry rooms, or basements, solid wood or moisture-resistant synthetic trim is generally preferred over standard MDF to prevent swelling and water damage over time.
acceptedAnswer.description: MDF is affordable, smooth, and great for painted, dry living areas, while solid wood holds up better against impacts and moisture in bathrooms or basements.
